fixes.current: mantenha o </text><emphasis>o</emphasis><text> final limpo. O brasileiro tende a levantar o "o" para "u" sem perceber (como em "gato" virando "gatu"). Aqui é "de" com "e" limpo, nunca "di".
fixes.fix: mantenha o </text><emphasis>e</emphasis><text> final limpo. O brasileiro tende a levantar o "e" final para "i" sem perceber (como em "leite" virando "leiti"). Aqui é "de", nunca "di".
fixes.why: Complaint is real. せいで and おかげで end in で, so the vowel at risk is the final "e", not "o"; the note contradicted itself one clause later ("Aqui e de com e limpo, nunca di"). Rewritten to teach the real pt-BR interference (final "e" raised to "i"), keeping the <emphasis> slot and the exact same tag multiset.

fixes.current: É comum fechar com から para reforçar: んだものだから ("porque... afinal").
fixes.fix: Para dar o motivo no meio da frase, use a forma simples + ものだから (na fala, もんだから). Ex.: 疲れていたものだから、先に帰った ("é que eu estava cansado, então fui embora antes"). Repare que んだもの fecha a frase e não recebe から.
fixes.why:
Complaint is real. んだもの is sentence-final and does not take から; the subordinate reason connector is plain form + ものだから / もんだから. The invented form んだものだから was being taught as a rule. Replacement keeps the identical tag multiset (1

, 3 , 2 ).

fixes.current: 出かけようとしたが、ところが雨が降ってきた
fixes.fix: 出かけようとしました。ところが雨が降ってきました
fixes.why: Complaint is real: this accepted variant glues ところが to a が-clause, exactly what the lesson warning note and this exercise own explanation forbid, and が plus ところが is redundant. This answer object is {text, accept}, not {choices, correct}, which is why the applier could not find the anchor. A mechanical applier cannot delete a list element safely, so the bad leaf is replaced in place by a legitimate polite-form variant of the same answer. The field path addresses the leaf string, never the answer object.

fixes.current: <item><jp reading="やすいにしてはおいしい">安いにしては美味しい</jp><text> = 'Para algo barato, é gostoso.'</text></item>
fixes.fix: <item><jp reading="こどもにしてはじがきれいだ">子どもにしては字がきれいだ</jp><text> = 'Para uma criança, a letra é muito bonita.'</text></item>
fixes.why: Complaint is real. にしては takes a noun or a plain-form verb, not an い-adjective, so 安いにしては is off-pattern; it also duplicated the meaning of the わりには example 値段の割にはおいしい that the same lesson uses later to contrast the two structures. Replaced by a concrete named base (子ども), which is what the lesson own rule demands. Same tag multiset.
